title: chiron viewer 1 — proposed UI map, keyboard-first, optimized for acquiring the substrate
purpose: Machine-readable target for the next viewer. Same shape as design/ui-map.json (surfaces, partitioning, components, textRoles, theme) so the two can be diffed, but every binding points at design/datamodel.json (entity.attribute) rather than at current web/ types. Non-inclusive: attributes the design does not surface are listed under notSurfaced with a reason. Where a surface needs data the pipeline does not yet expose, the entry carries a 'dependency'.

threeQuestions.phrasebook: How do I say it when instructing an agent?

principles: Entries are the unit of reading. Term, phrase, edge and chapter each get a full-width reading surface; the modal-only card is gone. The generated chapter markdown is replaced by a structured chapter entry built from the same substrate.
Dimensions are first-class navigation (keys 1-4), because the substrate answers three questions and the learner should be able to ask each one directly.
Type is chosen from contentKind, never from element name. One reconciled scale (16px base, ratio 1.2) across chrome and entry; the article/chrome split disappears with the vendored stylesheet.

Evidence is ink, not color. Anchor quotes are the only verbatim content; they are set in the reading face on the reading surface with a neutral rule and a provenance line. Color is reserved for two meanings: pine = you can act on this; amber = something drifted.

Keyboard focus is always visible and never ambiguous: exactly one pane owns focus (top-edge bar), exactly one row or reference is the cursor (ring), and selection (the open entry) is a background, so cursor and selection can differ.
Every cross-reference is reachable in two keystrokes from anywhere in an entry (f + hint letters), so following a thought never requires a mouse or a long tab walk.

Sections show identity, not content. Cross-reference lists (defines, mentions, phrasings, relations, neighborhood) carry only headwords — the reading text (definition, intent, gloss) is seen by an intentional act: peek, which always shows it in full, or opening the entry. Like flashcards: the corpus is recalled, not re-read. The index's one-line of meaning is the deliberate exception — it is the choosing surface.
Nothing renders below 4.5:1 text contrast in either theme; the pairs table is the allowed set, not a suggestion.
No uppercase labels. Hierarchy comes from size, weight, and color step, not from transform; headwords keep the corpus's own casing (datamodel: 'the corpus's spelling wins').

stack.framework: unchanged (Next.js App Router); routes below replace the chapter-only routing
stack.styling: global CSS custom properties; drop vendored github-markdown-css (no markdown surface remains)
stack.webfonts: one self-hosted variable serif is recommended (Source Serif 4 or equivalent); the map degrades to Iowan Old Style / Georgia without it. Sans and mono stay system.
stack.themeSwitch: [data-theme=light|dark] on <html> plus color-scheme; defaults to prefers-color-scheme; toggled by key t and persisted

layout.shell: rail (232px) | index (336px) | entry (fluid, reading measure 66ch) with a trail bar pinned above the entry pane. Panes are resizable; widths persisted. One pane owns keyboard focus at a time (2px --pine bar on its top edge). Adjacent panes are separated by a 1px --edge hairline (rail|index and index|entry) — the three surface tints are near-identical by design and need the rule to read as panes.
layout.trail: The dive stack made visible: a horizontal breadcrumb of entries visited by following cross-references (cap 16, as today). Backspace/u pops. Rendered above the entry, not inside it, so the entry's reading measure is never interrupted.
layout.entryMeasure: reading measure 66ch of the reading face at 16px, anchored at a fixed 640px so serif, sans and mono blocks share one right edge (ch resolves per element font); padding 48px 56px 96px; sections separated by 32px, not by rules

responsive.≤1100px: rail collapses to a 56px icon strip (dimension glyphs 1-4 + drift dot); index stays
responsive.≤880px: index and rail become overlays (as today); entry padding 32px 20px; type scale steps down one notch for the entry headword only (28→23); reading sizes never change

keymap.note: Global unless scoped. Arrow keys mirror h/j/k/l. The as-built IJKL/EDAF set can be kept as an alternate binding table.

within-pane.enter: open (index) / open the reference in place (entry — the same expanded window as space→enter; a reference's enter never navigates. f-hints and clicks are the travel gestures)

dimensions.note: 1-3 are keyboard-only: the rail displays no dimension rows (hidden by design — chapters are the primary navigation); dimensions are also reached via ⌘K and cross-references. 4 is the rail's only view row.

entry.f: hint mode: label every cross-reference and anchor with 1-2 letters; type the letters to follow (esc cancels)
entry.space: peek the cursor reference without leaving
entry.] / [: next / previous entry in the index without moving focus
entry.o: open chapter.source_url (or primary_path) in a new tab
entry.y: copy phrase.template (phrase entry) or term.term to clipboard

trail.shift+backspace: clear trail to the current entry

search./: filter the index (matches headword, aliases, slug)
search.⌘K / ctrl+K: jump anywhere (matches headword, aliases, slug, chapter title)

register.name + register.label per register, totals per implemented dimension using dimension.countNoun

surfaces.notes: Replaces corpora-index and register-hub. Recorded-mode marks live here (the rail shows no mode rows). Composition: page on --bg-index, one --paper card per register with a 1px --edge border and soft shadow — the cards are the only paper on the page.

displays: wordmark

corpus navigation: one row per mounted (corpus, register) — corpus.title + register.name (register.label on hover), active register highlighted; enter/click enters that register, landing on its chapters. The far-left pane navigates corpora entirely
Chapters row (key 4) with chapter count
drift summary: count of stale (chapter, dimension) pairs; enter opens the chapters index filtered to stale
surfaces.keyboard: 4 opens chapters; 1-3 switch dimensions without rail rows; 0 opens scope; the rail is a focusable pane (j/k over register rows, chapters, drift; enter activates)
surfaces.notes: Identity and corpus wayfinding only. Dimension rows are never displayed — chapters stay the primary navigation and the linguistic dimensions are reached through keys, jump, and cross-references. Groups are section headers inside the chapters index. Recorded modes are marked on the scope card, not here.

displays: lexicon: term.term + term.kind badge + one-line term.definition (truncated at 90 chars) + aliases as a muted second line when present; sorted alphabetically, or grouped by term.kind or by chapter.defines via the sort toggle
phrasebook: phrase.phrase + phrase.intent (one line); grouped by first term in phrase.terms or alphabetically
concept-relations: grouped by relationEdge.type (section header = type + count); row = from → to with gloss
chapters: grouped by group.label in register order; row = chapter.number + chapter.title + chapter.kind mark; per-dimension state dots appear only when some state ≠ ok — a clean row means healthy
filter field (/) with live count 'n of N'
surfaces.keyboard: j/k move the cursor, enter opens into entry, / filters, s cycles sort/grouping, esc clears filter
surfaces.notes: Identity plus one line of meaning per row: enough to choose without opening.

displays: term.term as headword with term.kind badge and term.slug
term.definition as the reading block
term.aliases as a plain run-in list ('Also written: …')
Defined in: chapter.title (cross-reference) via term.defined_in

Evidence: anchors deduped into quote-groups (anchors merge across chapters, so entries can carry 10-24 anchors with repeated quote text): one quote block per distinct quote, every distinct (chapter, path) provenance line beneath it, first-seen order; the first 6 groups render, the rest behind an expandable 'N more quotes' row (per-entry, not persisted). Drift marks per provenance line when anchor.curated_against ≠ chapter.content_hash
Phrasings: phrase.phrase cross-references only for each phrase whose terms include this slug — no intent run-in; peek or enter reveals it
Relations: outgoing and incoming relationEdge lists in two columns, edge type inline before the other-endpoint cross-reference — no gloss run-in; the edge entry and peek carry it
Mentioned in: derived chapter list
surfaces.keyboard: f hint mode (travel); n/p cycle references; e cycles anchors; space peeks; enter opens the reference in place; y copies term.term

displays: phrase.phrase as headword
phrase.intent as the reading block (one line, set at reading size)
phrase.template as a code block with {slots} highlighted; copy affordance (y)
Terms used: phrase.terms resolved to term.term chips with term.kind (cross-references)
Evidence: anchors as in entry-term
surfaces.keyboard: as entry-term; y copies the template

displays: headword line: from-term — type → to-term (both endpoints cross-references; type as label)
relationEdge.gloss as the reading block
type meaning from the closed relationType enum ('feeds: output of one becomes input of the other')
Evidence: anchors

Neighborhood: other edges sharing either endpoint, grouped under small type headings; rows never repeat the shared endpoint — a muted direction arrow (→ outgoing, ← incoming) + the other endpoint cross-reference only; the gloss is seen by peeking or following
surfaces.keyboard: as entry-term; [ ] step through edges of the same type

displays: chapter.title as headword with group.label · chapter.number as a muted sans meta beside it; the entry-kind badge appears only for kind=code; chapter.description as standfirst (markdown-stripped)
provenance block: chapter.unit_paths (primary_path first), chapter.source_url, chapter.content_hash

state per implemented dimension, quiet when healthy: one compact line (ok dots + 'all ok') when nothing is stale or none; the full per-dimension rows, stale anchor counts, and repair commands appear only on drift
Defines: term cross-references as a wrapped chip list (term + kind suffix) — no definitions; the learner peeks or opens a term to see it, like a flashcard
Mentions: terms anchored here but defined elsewhere, the same chip list
Phrasings grounded here (phrase cross-references only)
Relations anchored here: type + endpoint-pair cross-references, no gloss run-in (dependency: manifest must carry edges per chapter, not just a count)
surfaces.keyboard: as entry-term; o opens the source
surfaces.dependency: per-chapter edge list; anchor.path and curated_against exposed to the viewer
surfaces.notes: Replaces the generated-markdown article. Same information, typed per contentKind instead of flattened into bullets.

displays: compact (space): headword + kind, the full definition/intent/gloss (never clamped — the peek must fully view the reading text, which is what lets section lists omit it), first anchor quote, 'enter opens here'

expanded (enter): the full entry — every section, rendered exactly as the entry route renders it — in a centered scrollable overlay. The URL, index, and entry panes are untouched: a peek NEVER navigates, because a follow would replace the entry pane and switch the index dimension, invalidating the two panes behind it. References inside the card are real links — an explicit click travels and closes the overlay
surfaces.keyboard: space opens the compact peek; enter expands it in place — and enter directly on a reference cursor opens the expanded card without the compact step, so space→enter and enter land on the same window (enter on the expanded card closes); j/k scroll the expanded card; space/esc close
surfaces.notes: Compact is anchored beside the reference and never covers the reading measure; expanded is modal. Replaces the nested-modal dive — and carries the flashcard reveal: sections show identity, the peek shows content, and reading a whole entry in place is one more keystroke.

displays: single input; rows = kind glyph + headword + right detail (dimension · register); matches headword, aliases, slug, chapter title; aliases shown as the reason for the match
surfaces.keyboard: ⌘K opens; j/k or arrows; enter opens; esc closes
surfaces.notes: Fixes the alias gap: aliases are search keys.

displays: one prompt at a time from the current index scope: show phrase.intent → recall phrase.phrase; show term.definition → recall term.term; show from + to → recall relationEdge.type
reveal shows the answer with its first anchor as evidence
surfaces.keyboard: d starts; space reveals; j = got it, k = again; esc ends
surfaces.dependency: no persistence: datamodel notes quiz/progress state is unmodeled; the drill is stateless per session
surfaces.notes: Calibration is the learner's stated activity; this is the only surface that asks rather than shows.

partitioning.description: How the substrate is sliced across surfaces in this design

slices.scope: corpus + register identity, totals, provenance, worst-of state
slices.rail: mounted registers (title + name) as corpus navigation; chapter count; stale count — no dimension rows
slices.index: identity + one line of meaning per entry (headword, kind/type, definition|intent|gloss first line, aliases); state dots on chapters — the choosing surface keeps its one-liner
slices.entry-*: the full entry: every attribute the datamodel marks required, all anchors as deduped quote-groups (first 6 visible, rest expandable; e cycles visible groups), all inverse relationships as identity-only cross-reference lists (phrasings, edges, mentionedIn — no definition/intent/gloss run-ins)
slices.peek: headword + kind + the full reading text + first anchor — the flashcard reveal
slices.drill: one attribute pair per prompt, answer with one anchor

notSurfaced.dimension.dataFilename / methodologyDoc: tooling provenance; linked from help only
notSurfaced.mode.status for implemented modes: implied by being navigable; recorded modes are marked on the scope card (the rail shows no mode rows at all)
notSurfaced.term.definition / phrase.intent / relati: deliberately omitted — the peek shows the full text; seeing content is an intentional act (flashcards)
notSurfaced.corpus.origin: operational; scope shows checkout and urls instead
notSurfaced.cross-register views: no representation in the data model (datamodel modelingNotes)

textRoles.binds: corpus.title + register.name per mounted register | 'Chapters' + chapter count. Dimension rows are never rendered — this row style serves corpus navigation and the Chapters row only

spec.active: 600 + --sel bg + 3px left --dim-hue (register rows fall back to --pine)
spec.keycap: 11 mono in --edge box, right-aligned — Chapters row only (key 4)
spec.overflow: label never wraps the 32px row: nowrap + ellipsis

spec.marker: 3×12px rounded bar in --dim-hue before the label (the index-section consumer of the dimension hue)

spec.form: plain text after headword, no pill

spec.size: 7px circles, 3 in a row in registry order
spec.quietWhenOk: index chapter rows omit the dots entirely when every state is ok — health is the absence of marks, drift is the presence

textRoles.binds: term.kind | chapter.kind (code mark only — a chapter's group and number are muted sans meta beside the headword, never badged)

spec.placement: same line as kind, right of it

spec.note: the only block that may run multi-line at reading size; definition max 400 chars

spec.pattern: 'Also written' + comma list, run-in after the reading block

textRoles.binds: section names: Defined in, Evidence, Phrasings, Relations, Mentioned in, Terms used, Template, Provenance

spec.hangingPunct: opening quote hangs into the gutter
spec.codeVariant: quotes anchored into kind=code chapters are source text: mono 14/1.5, no typographic quotes, same rule
spec.note: reads as source text, not as a callout; the only verbatim block

spec.placement: below the quote, indented to the rule; one line per distinct (chapter, path) that pinned the quote
spec.chapter: quiet cross-reference: --ink-2 with tint underline, --pine only on cursor/hover — dozens of provenance lines must not out-shout the primary references

spec.mark: 6px --amber dot before the provenance line + 'pinned to 3f9a2c1d…, chapter now 7b02e4aa…'
spec.rule: left rule turns --amber for that quote only

textRoles.dependency: curated_against and content_hash exposed per anchor

textRoles.binds: any cross-reference to term / phrase / edge / chapter

spec.hintLabel: mono 11 --ink on --pine-tint, 2px radius, placed at the reference's start

textRoles.binds: phrase.phrase (cross-reference only — the intent lives in the peek and the phrase entry)
relationEdge grouped as outgoing / incoming — identity only, no gloss run-in (the edge entry and peek carry it)

spec.type: sans 13 500 --blue, inline before the endpoint — no fixed gutter, every line shares the measure's left edge

spec.copyHint: 'y copies' in 11 --muted, right-aligned above the block (never overlaid on the code)

textRoles.binds: phrase.terms | chapter.defines | chapter.mentions → term.term; the pill's color IS the kind (no kind text — the tooltip names it)

spec.face: serif 600 md; machine-literal kinds set mono 500 sm
spec.form: kind-coded pill: tinted background, 999px radius, 2px 10px, no underline (hover restores it); wrapped flex list with 8px gaps, no comma separators

kindHues.name: --plum on --plum-tint
kindHues.command / file / value: --ink-2 on --inset, mono — machine literals read as machine text

spec.note: every pair is in the contrast table; amber stays reserved for drift
the only amber block; sans, so it can never be confused with evidence

textRoles.binds: headword + kind + full reading text + first anchor

spec.reading: serif 15 1.5, full text — never clamped (field caps: definition 400, intent 160, gloss 200 chars, all fit the card)
spec.expanded: min(720px, 92vw), max-height 72vh scrollable, entry sections at their entry specs with 28/32/40 padding, footer above a hairline; its references live in their own scope (fresh registry) so the underlying entry's cursor and hints are untouched

textRoles.binds: headword + kind glyph + detail (dimension · register) + matched alias

spec.alias: sans 12 --ink-2 'also: …' when the match was an alias

spec.verdictKeys: keycaps j got it · k again

spec.tone: one sentence of what to do next

fonts.webfont: Source Serif 4 variable (opsz 8-60, wght 400-700), self-hosted, font-display: swap; used with opsz auto so small headwords in the index render at the text optical size and entry headwords at display

roleOfFaces.serif: what the corpus says: headwords, definitions, intents, glosses, quotes, drill prompts. Everything a learner reads to learn.
roleOfFaces.sans: what the viewer says: labels, counts, sections, meta, keys, status. Everything a learner reads to navigate.
roleOfFaces.mono: what the machine says: slugs, paths, hashes, templates, keycaps.

scale.note: one scale for the whole viewer; the chrome/article split is gone

contentKindStyles.prose: serif base/1.55, --ink, measure 640px (66ch of the reading face, fixed in px so mixed-font blocks share a right edge); index and peek use serif or sans at sm/md with clamp
contentKindStyles.headword: serif 600 at xxl (entry), md (index/chips), base (inline); never transformed; hyphenation off
contentKindStyles.label: sans 500-600 at sm, --ink-2 or --muted, sentence case, tracking ≤ .01em; badges only for term.kind and chapter.kind
contentKindStyles.identifier: mono at sm, --muted or --ink-2, white-space nowrap, no background
contentKindStyles.code: mono at 14 in a block on --inset with 4px radius; slots in --pine
contentKindStyles.quote: serif base/1.5, --ink, 2px --edge-strong left rule, hanging opening quote, provenance line below; no tint; rule turns --amber when the anchor is stale
contentKindStyles.count: sans tabular-nums at sm --muted; serif 500 at xxl for scope numerals

semantics.ink / ink-2 / muted: three-step text hierarchy (primary reading, secondary meaning, tertiary meta) — the as-built had two
semantics.pine: actionable: cross-references, focus ring, active pane bar, selected dimension, slots in templates
semantics.amber: drift only: stale dots, stale evidence rule, repair line. Never decorative.
semantics.plum / blue: dimension hues for phrasebook and concept-relations (lexicon is pine); used in the dimension indicators, kind glyphs and the entry kind badge — and reused as term-kind pill hues (name=plum, identifier=blue) in chip lists, where no dimension indicator shares the context, so the double duty stays legible
semantics.edge-strong: the evidence rule: neutral, because evidence is fact, not action or alarm
semantics.surfaces: rail (darkest neutral) → index → paper (entry): reading surface is always the brightest in light and the deepest in dark

pairs.note: WCAG 2.x contrast; only listed pairs may be used for text. Computed for the hex values above.
forbidden: --muted on --sel in dark for body text (4.2; use --ink-2)
--amber or --pine as a background for text other than --on-accent

consumers: rail Chapters row left bar when active (dimension rows are hidden; register rows use --pine)

states.paneFocus: 2px --pine bar across the top edge of the focused pane; unfocused panes show none
states.cursor: 2px --pine ring, inset on rows, 2px offset on inline references; moves without layout shift
states.selection: --sel background on the open entry's index row; persists when focus leaves the index
states.hintMode: 1-2 letter labels in mono 11 --ink on --pine-tint at the start of every reference and anchor; typed letters dim non-matching labels
states.hover: --hover background on rows; references gain a solid underline
states.focusVisible: the cursor ring doubles as :focus-visible; nothing else ever outlines

darkMode.mechanism: [data-theme] on <html>, color-scheme set to match, defaults to prefers-color-scheme, key t toggles and persists
darkMode.seams: none: a single stylesheet owns both schemes

motion.default: none; the trail's back/forward and peek open use a 120ms opacity/translate; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion

dependencies: chapter.description may contain inline markdown ([links](url), *emphasis*, `code`); the viewer strips the syntax for the standfirst rather than rendering it literally.

Anchors accumulate across chapters (mention anchors merge into the entry), so real entries exceed the 1-8 authoring cap with repeated quote text — the Evidence dedup + collapse policy above is load-bearing, not decorative.
Manifest must carry per-chapter relation edges (currently an edge count only) for entry-chapter 'Relations anchored here'.
anchor.path and anchor.curated_against must reach the viewer for evidence provenance and per-anchor drift marks.
Aliases must be included in the search index for jump and index filter.
Routes lexicon / phrasebook / relations / chapters reuse the reserved group ids the model already protects.
Drill state is unmodeled by design; if progress should persist, that is a data-model change, not a viewer one.
openQuestions: Whether to keep the IJKL/EDAF bindings as a selectable alternate layout or retire them.
Sorting default for the lexicon index: alphabetical (dictionary feel) vs by defining chapter (course feel).
Whether the peek should also work on index rows (preview without opening) — cheap to add, might make the entry pane feel optional.
